exercises.name: Cat-cow
exercises.setup: On hands and knees, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
exercises.steps: 1. Slowly round your back toward the ceiling and tuck your chin. 2. Then let your belly sink, lift your chest, and look slightly forward. 3. Move only as far as the motion stays comfortable.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain, radiating leg pain, or dizziness.
exercises.purpose: Gently moves the whole back through flexion and extension.

exercises.name: Child's pose
exercises.setup: Kneel, sit your hips toward your heels, and reach your arms forward on the floor.
exercises.steps: 1. Rest your forehead down. 2. Let your chest sink between your arms as you breathe. 3. Widen your knees if that lets the low back relax more.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp knee pain or a pinch in the low back.
exercises.purpose: Lengthens the back and gives the lumbar area a supported rest.

exercises.name: Band lat stretch
exercises.setup: Hold a light resistance band overhead with both hands, arms about shoulder-width apart.
exercises.steps: 1. Keep the ribs down and reach the band slightly up and back. 2. Side-bend a few inches to one side until you feel the opposite side of the back. 3. Return to center and repeat on the other side.
exercises.stop_if: You feel shoulder pinching or sharp pain under the arm.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the lat and the side of the mid-back.

exercises.name: Foam roller thoracic extension
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with a foam roller across the upper back, knees bent, and hands supporting your head.
exercises.steps: 1. Keep your ribs down. 2. Gently extend your upper back over the roller without cranking the neck. 3. Shift the roller up or down one segment and repeat.
exercises.dosage: 5 slow extensions at 3 spots on the upper back.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain, numbness, or pain that spreads into an arm.
exercises.purpose: Restores extension through the mid-back.

exercises.name: Peanut roller upper back
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with a peanut roller placed lengthwise on either side of the spine, not on the spine itself. Support your head with your hands.
exercises.steps: 1. Keep your neck relaxed. 2. Slowly extend over the peanut, then return. 3. Move it to the next spot between the shoulder blades and repeat.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pinch, dizziness, or arm symptoms.
exercises.purpose: Targets the muscles beside the thoracic spine more locally than a full foam roller.

exercises.name: Upper trapezius stretch
exercises.setup: Sit tall. Hold the chair with your right hand so the right shoulder stays down.
exercises.steps: 1. Tilt your left ear toward your left shoulder. 2. Keep the right shoulder heavy. 3. Add only a light touch from the left hand if you need a little more stretch.
exercises.stop_if: You feel tingling, dizziness, or pain shooting into the arm.
exercises.purpose: Eases tightness along the side of the neck into the top of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Levator scapulae stretch
exercises.setup: Sit tall and hold the chair with your right hand.
exercises.steps: 1. Turn your head about 45 degrees toward the left. 2. Tuck the chin toward the left armpit. 3. Keep the right shoulder down.
exercises.stop_if: You feel dizziness, sharp pain, or symptoms into the arm.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the muscle at the back corner of the neck.

exercises.name: Chin tucks
exercises.setup: Sit or stand with the back of your head in line with your spine, eyes looking forward.
exercises.steps: 1. Glide your chin straight back, as if making a double chin. 2. Do not tip the head up or down. 3. Hold briefly, then relax to the start.
exercises.stop_if: You feel dizziness, sharp pain, or increased headache.
exercises.purpose: Trains a less poked-forward neck position.

exercises.name: Neck rotation
exercises.setup: Sit tall with shoulders relaxed.
exercises.steps: 1. Turn your head slowly to the right until you feel a gentle stretch. 2. Return to center. 3. Repeat to the left.
exercises.stop_if: You feel dizziness, sharp pain, or symptoms traveling into the arm.
exercises.purpose: Keeps comfortable turning range in the neck.

exercises.name: Scalene stretch
exercises.setup: Sit tall and hold the chair with your right hand.
exercises.steps: 1. Tip your left ear toward your left shoulder. 2. Then rotate your chin slightly up toward the ceiling. 3. Keep the right shoulder down and the stretch mild.
exercises.stop_if: You feel tingling, dizziness, or a strong pull at the front of the neck.
exercises.purpose: Gently lengthens the muscles at the front and side of the neck.

exercises.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
exercises.setup: Sit or stand tall with the right arm relaxed across your chest.
exercises.steps: 1. Use the left hand to draw the right arm closer to the chest. 2. Keep the right shoulder down, not shrugged. 3. Repeat on the other arm.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a pinch in the front or top of the shoulder.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the back of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Wall pec stretch
exercises.setup: Stand beside a wall. Place your forearm on the wall with the elbow a little below shoulder height.
exercises.steps: 1. Step the same-side foot forward. 2. Gently turn your chest away from the wall until you feel the front of the shoulder and chest. 3. Keep the stretch mild and repeat on the other side.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a pinch deep in the front of the shoulder or tingling in the hand.
exercises.purpose: Opens the chest and the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Band external rotation
exercises.setup: Elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked at your side. Hold a light resistance band in the outside hand, with the other end fixed or held in front of you.
exercises.steps: 1. Keep the elbow pinned to your side. 2. Rotate the forearm outward, away from the belly. 3. Return slowly.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pinch in the shoulder or pain into the neck.
exercises.purpose: Strengthens the rotator cuff muscles that steady the shoulder.

exercises.name: Dumbbell scaption raise
exercises.setup: Stand tall holding a very light dumbbell in one hand, thumb slightly up.
exercises.steps: 1. Raise the arm on a diagonal, about halfway between in front and out to the side. 2. Stop around shoulder height. 3. Lower slowly and repeat, then switch arms.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a pinch at the top of the shoulder or need to shrug to lift the weight.
exercises.purpose: Builds control of the shoulder in a commonly comfortable raise path.

exercises.name: Peanut roller front shoulder
exercises.setup: Lie face up with a peanut roller placed under the front of one shoulder, at the chest-shoulder junction, not on the neck.
exercises.steps: 1. Let that arm rest out to the side. 2. Breathe and allow the chest to soften over the roller. 3. Shift slightly if you find a tender spot, then switch sides.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain, numbness, or tingling into the hand.
exercises.purpose: Releases the front of the shoulder and upper chest.

exercises.name: Figure-four stretch
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with both knees bent. Cross the right ankle over the left thigh.
exercises.steps: 1. Draw the left thigh toward your chest. 2. Keep the right knee open, away from the midline. 3. Hold, then switch sides.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp groin, knee, or low-back pain.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the glute on the crossed-leg side.

exercises.name: 90/90 hip stretch
exercises.setup: Sit on the floor with the front knee bent about 90 degrees in front of you and the back knee bent about 90 degrees out to the side.
exercises.steps: 1. Sit tall over the front shin. 2. Hinge slightly forward until you feel the front-side glute. 3. Switch the leg positions and repeat.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a pinch in the front of the hip or sharp knee pain.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the glutes and changes hip rotation.

exercises.name: Band glute bridge
exercises.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Place a resistance band just above the knees.
exercises.steps: 1. Gently press the knees out into the band. 2. Lift the hips until the body is a straight line from shoulders to knees. 3. Lower with control.
exercises.stop_if: You feel cramping in the low back or sharp hip pain.
exercises.purpose: Wakes up the glutes so they share work with the low back.

exercises.name: Foam roller glutes
exercises.setup: Sit on a foam roller with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee. Support yourself with your hands behind you.
exercises.steps: 1. Shift your weight toward the crossed-leg glute. 2. Roll slowly a few inches, pausing on tender spots. 3. Switch sides.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain or tingling down the leg.
exercises.purpose: Reduces local glute tightness.

exercises.name: Band clamshell
exercises.setup: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent about 45 degrees. Place a resistance band just above the knees.
exercises.steps: 1. Keep your feet together and your pelvis still. 2. Lift the top knee without rolling backward. 3. Lower slowly, then switch sides.
exercises.stop_if: You feel low-back pain or the motion is only happening by rolling the trunk.
exercises.purpose: Strengthens the side glute that controls the hip.

exercises.name: Standing calf stretch
exercises.setup: Face a wall. Step one foot back, heel down, knee straight. The front knee is softly bent.
exercises.steps: 1. Lean toward the wall until you feel the back calf. 2. Keep the back heel on the floor and the toes pointing forward. 3. Switch legs.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pull at the Achilles tendon or pain in the heel.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the larger calf muscle with the knee straight.

exercises.name: Bent-knee calf stretch
exercises.setup: Use the same wall stance as a calf stretch, but bend the back knee slightly while the heel stays down.
exercises.steps: 1. Shift weight forward. 2. Keep the heel planted so the stretch sits lower in the calf. 3. Switch legs.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp Achilles or heel pain.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the deeper calf muscle.

exercises.name: Band ankle dorsiflexion
exercises.setup: Sit with one leg straight. Loop a resistance band around the forefoot and hold the ends.
exercises.steps: 1. Pull the band so it assists the foot pulling up toward you. 2. Actively lift the foot as well. 3. Lower slowly and repeat, then switch feet.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pinch at the front of the ankle.
exercises.purpose: Improves the ankle bend the calf limits.

exercises.name: Foam roller calves
exercises.setup: Sit with one calf on a foam roller and hands on the floor behind you.
exercises.steps: 1. Roll slowly from just below the knee to above the Achilles. 2. Keep the pressure tolerable. 3. Switch legs.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp tendon pain or numbness in the foot.
exercises.purpose: Eases tight calf muscle.

exercises.name: Dumbbell calf raise
exercises.setup: Stand holding a light dumbbell in one hand. Use the other hand on a wall for balance.
exercises.steps: 1. Rise onto the balls of both feet. 2. Pause briefly at the top. 3. Lower the heels slowly.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp Achilles pain or cannot lower the heel with control.
exercises.purpose: Strengthens the calves through a full, slow range.

exercises.name: Supine band hamstring stretch
exercises.setup: Lie on your back. Loop a resistance band around one foot and hold the ends.
exercises.steps: 1. Keep that knee mostly straight. 2. Use the band to guide the leg up until you feel the back of the thigh. 3. Keep the opposite leg resting down. Switch sides.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain behind the knee or pain spreading below the knee.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the hamstring without forcing the leg up by hand.

exercises.name: Standing hamstring hinge
exercises.setup: Stand with one heel forward, toes up, and that knee softly straight. The back knee is slightly bent.
exercises.steps: 1. Hinge at the hips and reach the chest toward the front shin. 2. Keep the back flat rather than rounding hard. 3. Switch legs.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pull behind the knee or low-back pain.
exercises.purpose: Lengthens the hamstring in a standing hip hinge.

exercises.name: Seated hamstring stretch
exercises.setup: Sit on the front of a chair with one leg straight, heel on the floor.
exercises.steps: 1. Sit tall, then hinge forward from the hips toward the straight leg. 2. Stop when the back of the thigh stretches. 3. Switch legs.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp knee pain or symptoms down the leg.
exercises.purpose: A supported hamstring stretch for people who do not want to get on the floor.

exercises.name: Foam roller hamstrings
exercises.setup: Sit with the back of one thigh on a foam roller and your hands behind you.
exercises.steps: 1. Roll slowly from just below the sit bone to just above the knee. 2. Skip the knee itself. 3. Switch legs.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain, bruising-level pressure, or tingling.
exercises.purpose: Loosens the hamstring muscle belly.

exercises.name: Dumbbell hip hinge
exercises.setup: Hold a light dumbbell in both hands in front of your thighs. Feet about hip-width apart, knees softly bent.
exercises.steps: 1. Push the hips back and lower the dumbbell along the legs. 2. Stop when the hamstrings stretch and the back is still long. 3. Stand by driving the hips forward.
exercises.stop_if: You feel low-back pain or cannot keep the spine long.
exercises.purpose: Teaches the hamstrings to load in a hinge instead of the low back.

exercises.name: Prayer stretch
exercises.setup: Sit or stand and place your palms together in front of your chest.
exercises.steps: 1. Keeping the palms together, lower the hands until you feel the forearms. 2. Do not force the heels of the hands apart. 3. Hold, then shake the hands out.
exercises.frequency: 2 times a day, especially after typing.
exercises.stop_if: You feel numbness, sharp wrist pain, or tingling in the fingers.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the wrist flexors on the palm side of the forearm.

exercises.name: Wrist extensor stretch
exercises.setup: Hold one arm straight in front of you, palm down.
exercises.steps: 1. Use the other hand to gently bend the wrist so the fingers point down. 2. Keep the elbow soft, not locked. 3. Switch hands.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp wrist pain or tingling in the fingers.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the muscles on the back of the forearm.

exercises.name: Tendon glides
exercises.setup: Rest the forearm on a table, palm up, wrist straight.
exercises.steps: 1. Start with the hand open. 2. Bend the fingertips to the top of the palm, then make a loose fist, then a full fist. 3. Open the hand again and repeat.
exercises.stop_if: You feel catching pain, numbness, or a sharp pull in a finger.
exercises.purpose: Moves the finger tendons through the hand and wrist.

exercises.name: Band finger extension
exercises.setup: Place a light resistance band around the fingers and thumb of one hand, near the tips.
exercises.steps: 1. Open the hand against the band. 2. Pause when the fingers are spread. 3. Return slowly and switch hands.
exercises.stop_if: You feel pain in a finger joint or cramping that does not ease when you stop.
exercises.purpose: Strengthens the muscles that open the hand.

exercises.name: Peanut roller forearm
exercises.setup: Place a peanut roller on a table. Rest one forearm on it, palm down.
exercises.steps: 1. Roll slowly from just above the wrist to just below the elbow. 2. Turn the palm up and roll the other side of the forearm. 3. Switch arms.
exercises.dosage: 30 seconds each side of each forearm.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain, bruising pressure, or tingling in the hand.
exercises.purpose: Eases tight forearm muscles that pull on the wrist and hand.

exercises.name: Plantar fascia stretch
exercises.setup: Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
exercises.steps: 1. Hold the toes of the crossed foot. 2. Gently pull them back toward the shin until you feel the arch. 3. Switch feet.
exercises.frequency: 2 times a day, including before first steps.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp tear-like pain in the arch or heel.
exercises.purpose: Stretches the tissue along the sole of the foot.

exercises.name: Ankle circles
exercises.setup: Sit with one foot off the floor.
exercises.steps: 1. Draw slow circles with the foot, leading from the ankle. 2. Keep the motion smooth. 3. Reverse direction, then switch feet.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pinch at the ankle or pain up the shin.
exercises.purpose: Moves the ankle through its available range.

exercises.name: Toe spreads
exercises.setup: Sit with both feet flat on the floor.
exercises.steps: 1. Lift the toes, then try to spread them apart. 2. Place them back down without gripping. 3. If the small toes will not move, use your fingers to guide them once, then try again.
exercises.stop_if: You feel cramping that lingers or sharp pain in the forefoot.
exercises.purpose: Restores control of the toes and the front of the foot.

exercises.name: Band ankle inversion and eversion
exercises.setup: Sit with a resistance band looped around the forefoot. Hold the band so it resists the motion you are practicing.
exercises.steps: 1. For inversion, turn the sole inward against the band. 2. For eversion, turn the sole outward against the band. 3. Move slowly and switch feet.
exercises.stop_if: You feel sharp pain on either side of the ankle.
exercises.purpose: Strengthens the muscles that steady the ankle and foot.

exercises.name: Foam roller arch
exercises.setup: Stand and place one foot on a foam roller, roller running across the arch.
exercises.steps: 1. Put only light pressure through that foot. 2. Roll slowly from the heel pad toward the ball of the foot, staying off the toes. 3. Switch feet.
exercises.stop_if: You feel a sharp pain in the arch or heel.
exercises.purpose: Gently loosens the sole of the foot.
